topic: Instantaneous Rate of Change and the Derivative

outline.topic: Instantaneous Rate of Change and the Derivative

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Average Rate of Change
sections.content: Define average rate of change as the slope of a secant line between two points (x, f(x)) and (x+h, f(x+h)). Use a visual of a car traveling between two points on a road to show the concept of 'average speed'.
sections.example: A cheetah runs from point A to point B. Average speed = total distance / total time.

sections.title: The Conceptual Bridge: Shrinking the Interval
sections.content: Animate the second point moving closer to the first point (h approaches 0). Visually demonstrate how the secant line transforms into a tangent line. Introduce the concept that as 'h' gets smaller, the average rate of change approaches the 'instantaneous' rate.
sections.example: Visualize the cheetah's journey: instead of calculating speed over 1 hour, we calculate it over 1 minute, then 1 second, then a millisecond.

sections.title: Formal Definition: The Derivative
sections.content: Introduce the formal limit definition: f'(x) = lim(h→0) [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h. Explain this as the slope of the tangent line at a specific point, which represents the instantaneous rate of change.
sections.example: A motion tracker on the cheetah displaying the exact speedometer reading at the precise moment it reaches a specific tree.

sections.title: Application: Visualizing the Slope
sections.content: Show a graph of a non-linear function (a parabola). Move a tangent line along the curve, demonstrating how the slope (derivative value) changes dynamically. This connects algebraic limits to geometric reality.
sections.example: A drone pilot monitoring the climb rate of their craft; the derivative is the real-time vertical speed shown on the controller display.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
sections.content: Recap: Derivative = slope of the tangent = instantaneous rate of change. Remind students that the derivative is the 'limit' of the average rate of change as the interval disappears.
sections.example: Final infographic comparing the 'average' (broad span) vs. the 'derivative' (the exact snapshot moment).

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Average Rate of Change
lecture_lines: Average rate is the slope of a secant line.
It measures change over an interval of time.
Think of speed over a distance. [Asset: secant_line_anim]
animations: Draw a secant line between two points (a, f(a)) and (a+h, f(a+h)). Label points and line.
Label the slope as [f(a+h) - f(a)] / h using color #FFFFFF.
Highlight the points in color #FF00FF and the line in #00FFFF.

storyboard.title: The Conceptual Bridge: Shrinking the Interval
lecture_lines: What happens if the interval gets smaller?
The secant line approaches the tangent line.
As h nears zero, we find instantaneous rate. [Asset: shrinking_h_anim]
animations: Show points (a, f(a)) and (a+h, f(a+h)) on a curve.
Animate the point (a+h, f(a+h)) moving towards (a, f(a)).
Show the secant line flattening into a tangent line.

storyboard.title: Formal Definition: The Derivative
lecture_lines: This is the formal definition of a derivative.
It is the limit of the difference quotient.
The slope at a single point. [Asset: limit_definition_anim]
It captures the instantaneous rate of change.
A precise measurement at one moment. [Asset: speedometer_anim]
animations: Display limit notation: lim as h goes to 0.
Show the fraction [f(a+h) - f(a)] / h beside the limit.
Highlight the resulting expression f'(a) in color #FFFF00.

storyboard.title: Application: Visualizing the Slope
lecture_lines: Observe the slope changing along the curve.
The derivative is the tangent line's slope.
This connects algebra to geometry. [Asset: tangent_slider_anim]
Like a drone measuring climb rate.
Instantaneous changes visualized in real time. [Asset: climb_rate_anim]
animations: Display a graph of a function with varying slopes.
Highlight tangent lines at different points in color #00FF00.
Show slope values change smoothly as a tangent point moves.

storyboard.title: Summary and Conclusion
lecture_lines: Derivative is the tangent line's slope.
It measures the instantaneous rate of change.
It is the limit of average rate. [Asset: summary_chart_anim]
Average rate over an interval.
Derivative at a specific point. [Asset: comparison_infographic_anim]
animations: Summarize: Secant slope approaches tangent slope at a point.
Display f'(a) as the limit of the difference quotient.
Flash all key formula components in color #FFFFFF.
